cooling.curve.auto.deadband.help: How far below the target counts as close enough, so the fans are not adjusted over a fraction of a degree.
cooling.curve.auto.hint: Aims to hold a target temperature: ramps between the idle and load points, then nudges the speed up or down in small steps once the load point is reached.
cooling.curve.auto.speed.help: The range this curve is allowed to work in. It never asks for less than the first or more than the second.
cooling.curve.auto.step.help: How much duty each adjustment adds once the target is reached. Steps down are half this, so it backs off gently.
cooling.curve.auto.temp.help: Idle is the temperature the fans can stay at their minimum for; the second is the temperature this curve tries to hold. The gap between them must be larger than the deadband.
cooling.curve.fixed.hint: Hold a constant duty regardless of temperature.
cooling.curve.fixed.speed.help: The duty every fan on this curve holds, whatever the temperature does.
cooling.curve.graph.hint: Custom multi-point shape. Drag points to adjust, double-click to add, right-click to remove.
cooling.curve.linear.hint: Ramp duty smoothly between a min and max temperature.
cooling.curve.linear.speed.help: The duty at each end of that temperature band; everything between is a straight line.
cooling.curve.linear.temp.help: The band the ramp covers: below the first the fans sit at their minimum, above the second at their maximum.
cooling.curve.mix.fn.help: How the curves below combine: the quietest of them, the loudest, or their average.
cooling.curve.mix.hint: Combines multiple input curves into one output. Pick how their values blend - minimum (quietest), maximum (coolest), or average - and the result drives the fans bound to this curve. Useful when one fan should react to several temperature sources at once.
cooling.curve.response.help: How quickly the fan follows a change: longer smooths out short spikes, shorter reacts immediately.
cooling.curve.source.help: The temperature this curve watches. The fans on it react to this reading and nothing else.
cooling.curve.sync.hint: Follows another fan, either at a percentage of its speed or a fixed number of points above or below it.
cooling.curve.sync.offset.help: How far this curve sits from the fan it follows: a share of that fan's duty in percent mode, or a fixed number of points.
cooling.curve.sync.source.help: The fan this curve copies. It follows that fan's duty, whatever is driving it.
cooling.curve.trigger.hint: Two speeds and nothing in between: steps up once the temperature stays above the load point, back down once it stays below the idle point, and holds whatever it last chose in the gap.
cooling.curve.trigger.speed.help: The two duties this curve switches between, one for idle and one for load.
cooling.curve.trigger.temp.help: The two thresholds: crossing the upper one steps the fans up, dropping below the lower steps them back down. In between they hold.

site.about.p1: Vendor software for PC hardware is heavy, closed, and stops at the edge of its own brand. We wanted one fast app that treats your whole system - every fan, sensor, and LED - as one, no matter who made the parts.
site.about.p2: So we built Nexus: open source, native, and designed with the same care as the hardware it drives. It runs on your system, your data stays yours, and the community shapes where it goes next.
site.about.title: Why we built Nexus

site.cooling.lead: Draw your own fan curves and Nexus holds every fan and pump to them, driven by any temperature sensor in your system. This is the real curve editor from the app.

site.cooling.point2: Mixed sources, hysteresis, and smooth ramping
site.cooling.point3: Profiles for silent, balanced, and full-tilt
